title: Autopilot Update: More Control Over Borrower Requests & Expanded Review Checks | Blend
summary: Lenders get more control over borrower requests, plus automated pre-underwriting checks for cash to close, credit events, and hourly income.
body_markdown:
Pre-underwriting works best when it fits the way each lender already runs its pipeline. Lenders decide when a file stops taking new document requests, which requests belong to the loan officer, and how many times a borrower should be asked for the same thing. And the more a file is checked before it reaches underwriting, the fewer surprises the underwriter finds.


This week’s updates build on both. Autopilot gives lenders more control over borrower requests and leaves follow-up on lender-created requests to the loan officer instead of asking the borrower again. Autopilot also expands its review of cash to close, bankruptcy and foreclosure waiting periods, and hourly income.


## In beta: Autopilot honors milestone rules before creating borrower requests


Lenders can use milestone rules to pause new document requests at stages they choose. Autopilot now checks those rules before it creates each request. Requests covered by a rule aren’t sent to the borrower or added to the loan officer’s suggestions. Any exceptions the lender has configured still apply.


Autopilot checks the loan’s current milestone each time it reviews the loan, so a rule takes effect at the first review after the milestone changes.


For example, say a loan reaches clear to close, where the lender has paused new requests. If the borrower later uploads another document, Autopilot reviews it but holds back any new requests covered by the rule. This feature is in beta. To enable it, contact your Blend account team.


### Subscribe to Autopilot updates


## Fewer repeat borrower requests, with follow-up left to the lender


Autopilot leaves follow-ups to the loan officer when an upload doesn’t satisfy a request the lender created. For example, if a loan officer requests a signed gift letter and the borrower uploads an unsigned copy, Autopilot leaves the upload for the loan officer to review and follow up on. Navigator won’t resend requests the lender removed.


When a borrower uploads the wrong document, Autopilot asks again once by default, then hands the request to the loan team. Lenders can change how many times Autopilot re-asks, or turn re-asks off, by contacting their Blend account team.


Together, these changes reduce repeat asks while keeping lenders in control of their own requests.


## Expanded checks before underwriting


### Cash to close


When the Closing Disclosure shows cash due from the borrower, Autopilot asks for asset documents to cover that amount, even if the application lists no accounts. For example, if a refinance Closing Disclosure shows money due to the borrower, Autopilot doesn’t look for sourced funds. On a purchase where the borrower needs to bring money to closing, it looks for documentation of the required funds.


### Bankruptcy and foreclosure


When a borrower discloses a bankruptcy, foreclosure, deed-in-lieu or short sale on the application, Autopilot asks for the documents the program’s guidelines require, such as discharge papers, instead of relying on the dates the borrower entered.


### Hourly income


Autopilot can now read the hourly pay rate from a VOE or paystub, so base income can be calculated as rate × hours when the guidelines call for that method.


These checks help surface items before the file reaches underwriting. Findings remain subject to review by the loan officer or underwriter.
